results.explanation: At the declared POST /process/text entry, the caller is supplied through get_verified_user. When a caller-selected collection name is present, the endpoint invokes _validate_collection_access with access_type='write' before constructing the document and calling save_docs_to_vector_db. That validator delegates to filter_accessible_collections, whose non-admin knowledge-base path adds the name only when Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id(name, user.id, permission='write') succeeds; otherwise an existing knowledge base is not admitted by the fallback for nonexistent knowledge bases. Under the stated premise that the selected collection exists and the verified non-admin has neither ownership nor an explicit write grant, the name is denied, _validate_collection_access raises 403, and the vector-database write sink is not reached. Therefore the source-visible behavior at the declared-entry boundary is deny.

async def _validate_collection_access(collection_names: list[str], user, access_type: str = 'read') -> None:
    """
    Raise 403 if the user lacks access to any of the requested collections.
    Delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections utility so the
    access rules stay in one place.
    """
    requested = set(collection_names)
    allowed = await filter_accessible_collections(requested, user, access_type=access_type)
    denied = requested - allowed
    if denied:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )
